# zuarrow

DuckDB, Polars, ADBC drivers, pyarrow and the arrow package all hand
data around as [Apache Arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/) columns. R has
no exact form for several of Arrow’s types: a 64-bit integer past 2^53,
a `decimal128`, a nanosecond timestamp. The usual bridges convert them
to a double anyway, and the change goes unnoticed until a join key no
longer matches.

zuarrow moves columns between R and Arrow on one rule: **a value crosses
exactly, or the call fails**, naming the column and the R type that
would hold it.

- **Exact or error.** `lossy = "error"` is the default everywhere. Ask
  for the exact text, the nearest R type with a warning, or the nearest
  R type silently, but only by asking.
- **A registry for exact types.** A package registers its class for an
  Arrow type with
  [`arrow_register()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_register.md),
  and from then on that column converts exactly.
- **Both IPC formats.**
  [`arrow_read()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_read.md)
  and
  [`arrow_write()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_write.md)
  handle the file (`.arrow`, Feather version 2) and the stream
  (`.arrows`), with LZ4 and zstd bodies decompressed by
  [zukomp](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zukomp), so a compressed file
  opens on every machine.
- **Hostile input is refused, not trusted.** Every message is checked
  against limits before it is used and every batch is fully validated.
  The reader is fuzzed and checked against Arrow’s own conformance
  files.
- **nanoarrow’s handles.** zuarrow’s schemas, arrays and streams are
  [nanoarrow](https://arrow.apache.org/nanoarrow/)’s, so they pass
  between the two packages without conversion.

## Installation

zuarrow is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuarrow")
```

## Usage

``` r

library(zuarrow)
```

Ordinary columns cross both ways unchanged, factors and dates included.

``` r

df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3,
  city = factor(c("Lisbon", "Porto", "Lisbon")),
  day = as.Date("2026-10-21") + 0:2
)
identical(arrow_to_r(arrow_array(df)), df)
#> [1] TRUE
```

A 64-bit integer that a double cannot hold is an error, not a rounding.

``` r

big <- arrow_array(c("9007199254740993", "1"), schema = "l")
arrow_to_r(big)
#> Error in `arrow_to_r()`:
#> ! Column 1 (Arrow format `l`) cannot be converted to R exactly: row 1 holds 9007199254740993. Load zuint to read it exactly, or use `lossy = "character"` for its exact text, or `lossy = "allow"` to accept the loss.
```

`lossy = "character"` gives the exact text, which writes back to the
same type.

``` r

text <- arrow_to_r(big, lossy = "character")
text
#> [1] "9007199254740993" "1"               
#> attr(,"arrow_type")
#> [1] "l"
arrow_equal(arrow_array(text), big)
#> [1] TRUE
```

The IPC formats are one call each way, with compression on request.

``` r

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".arrow")
arrow_write(df, path, compression = "zstd")
arrow_read(path)
#>   id   city        day
#> 1  1 Lisbon 2026-10-21
#> 2  2  Porto 2026-10-22
#> 3  3 Lisbon 2026-10-23
```

Apart from
[`zuarrow_info()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/zuarrow_info.md),
every function is prefixed `arrow_`. Each takes or returns a handle or a
plain R object. zuarrow’s own errors inherit from `zuarrow_error`, with
a class for each kind, such as `zuarrow_lossy_error`.

## Learn more

- [Receiving a DuckDB result without
  rounding](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/articles/duckdb.html)
  shows the headline use.
- The [reference](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/) lists
  every function;
  [`arrow_types()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_types.md)
  prints the type table.

## Related work

zuarrow bundles the
[nanoarrow](https://github.com/apache/arrow-nanoarrow) C library and is
checked against
[apache/arrow-testing](https://github.com/apache/arrow-testing)’s IPC
golden files and crash corpus, and against the arrow package.

# Package index

## Handles

Schemas, arrays and streams in the layout nanoarrow uses, built from R
objects or accepted from any Arrow producer.

- [`arrow_schema()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_schema.md)
  : Arrow schemas
- [`arrow_array()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_array.md)
  [`arrow_stream()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_array.md)
  : Build an Arrow array or stream from R

## Back to R

Exact conversion to R vectors and data frames, or an error.

- [`arrow_to_r()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_to_r.md)
  [`arrow_next()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_to_r.md)
  : Convert Arrow data to R
- [`arrow_matrix()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_matrix.md)
  : Matrices as fixed-size lists

## The IPC formats

The Arrow file and stream formats, plain or compressed.

- [`arrow_read()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_read.md)
  : Read the Arrow IPC formats
- [`arrow_write()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_write.md)
  : Write the Arrow IPC formats
- [`arrow_limits()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_limits.md)
  : Limits on IPC input

## Validation, comparison and metadata

- [`arrow_validate()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_validate.md)
  : Validate an array or stream
- [`arrow_equal()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_equal.md)
  : Compare two schemas, arrays or streams
- [`arrow_metadata()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_metadata.md)
  [`` `arrow_metadata<-`() ``](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_metadata.md)
  : Schema metadata

## The registry

Which R class is the exact form of which Arrow type.

- [`arrow_register()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_register.md)
  [`arrow_unregister()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_register.md)
  [`arrow_registry()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_register.md)
  : Register an exact R type for an Arrow type
- [`arrow_types()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/arrow_types.md)
  : The built-in type table
- [`zuarrow_info()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuarrow/reference/zuarrow_info.md)
  : Package information
